issue_context.title: Remove Roslyn-Reflection helper abstraction from System.Text.Json source generator
issue_context.body:
This issue refers to the helpers here: https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/tree/5a5ab5962e20d10718b326dda56dfc9285be9acf/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/gen/Reflection.

These helpers provide a conversion from Roslyn metadata to Reflection metadata. They predated the JSON generator (developed by @davidfowl), and were copied into the initial version of the source generator for the following reasons:

- The developers were more familiar with Reflection APIs and could make progress more expeditiously with the abstraction
- There was an expectation that there would be a non-trivial amount of Reflection-based code shared between the source-generator and reflection-based implementations of `JsonSerializer`.

Both reasons no longer hold. The amount/utility of the [code shared](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/5a5ab5962e20d10718b326dda56dfc9285be9acf/src/libraries/System.Text.Json/Common/ReflectionExtensions.cs) between the implementations does not justify the additional complexity to maintain the abstraction. There's no good reason to not read the metadata from Roslyn APIs directly.

Likely not tbh. I'm fine with making this "future".

review_comments: Is this part of the algorithm the same as the reflection implementation?
Yes. It's just linear traversal of the superclass hierarchy.
nit: was wondering if it should be moved into the shared helper.
It's much simpler to express compared to topological sorting, so extracting an abstraction out of it isn't worth the hassle in my view.
Why not maintain an abstraction for both symbols and `Type`s, similar to `TraverseGraphWithTopologicalSort`?

The sorting function only needs a graph abstraction to function, so it's fairly straightforward to generalize. This method on the other hand depends on many things, including querying for constructor methods, accessibility modifiers and arities. It is introducing a bit of duplication but that's probably fine (most other logic in the parser is already duplicating logic from the reflection serializer).
Well I guess the duplication is fine if there's not much further churn.
Were these tests running prior to this change?
I believe they were not. Luckily they were still passing :-)
Is there a pragma warning still?
Unfortunately, yes. It's a false positive in the analyzer tracked by the linked issue.
Oh I asked because the issue is closed. I I see now that it was fixed for a later version of Roslyn and our 3.11 / 4.0 projects still need the suppression.
Does this fix a bug?

I've moved the FQN formatting to use Roslyn's built-in `SymbolDisplayFormat.FullyQualifiedFormat`, but that actually renders tuple types as `(int, string, bool)` instead of `ValueTuple<int, string, bool>`. This ends up breaking the parameterless constructor emitter because `new (int, string, bool)()` is not valid. I've included this flag to account for the issue.
Should these two helpers be in `RoslynExtensions`?
It depends on a number of symbols that are cached by this class, so it wouldn't be practical to define as an extension method.
Why's this generic? The same type arguments are being used for both calls AFAICT.
It's not a bound to a particular type. The parameters could have just been `object`, however I wanted a way to ensure that both arguments are of the same type.
https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/86334#discussion_r1196803863
Replaces the algorithm now deleted from ReflectionExtensions.cs to one that better works for both Symbol and Type instances.
Do we have equivalent coverage for all applicable tests in this suite?

Mostly they're there to validate the implementation of the type implementations, however there seems to be one test that does a lot of generic testing which I salvaged and moved to the main test suite (FWIW similar tests already exist in the main test project).
Should the string formatting of the default value happen here instead of the emitter stage?

Are you asking because the default is of type `object`? Because default method parameters can only be literals they should still behave fine w.r.t. caching. Besides, formatting should be the responsibility of the emitter in general.
👍 for both points.
This is doing a ton of lookups on construction.  Are the majority of them needed on any given use?  I'm wondering if they should be lazy instead.

> Are the majority of them needed on any given use?

Mostly, yes. There are exceptions, e.g. the attribute type symbols could be skipped in type graphs with no annotations but comparably speaking they're not many.

FWIW this isn't changing the resolution semantics of these symbols, it simply moves them to a dedicated class. The plan is to eventually put this in an incremental value, so that each generated `JsonSerializerContext` can reference it independently and on-demand.
cc @layomia this implements the pattern you've been using in the ConfigurationBinder source generator.
Why do this?

We don't want to generate metadata for both `JsonTypeInfo<(string x, int)>` and `JsonTypeInfo<(string?, int)>`, since at runtime they are the same type (`JsonSerializerContext` looks up metadata by `Type`). Wrapping the symbols inside a `Type` abstraction meant that these differences went away, however when handling raw compile-time symbols you need to use a normal form.
Oh is this why we trim type symbol metadata? Would we need to generate metadata for both if we switch to emitting `enable nullable`?
Correct, compile-time metadata needs to be trimmed regardless of nullability annotation (tuple labels are independent of them).
Is this to be merged with `TypeGenerationSpec`?
It's intended as a lightweight identity token, separate to `TypeGenerationSpec`. This way you can include references to types in property specs without worrying about cycles or stack overflows.

I wonder if the increased concept count is worth it & if the previous approach of guarding the recursion with caching logic in the parser suffices. Maybe the `TypeRef` token would feel more natural with a different name.

The problem is that recursive/cyclical models don't work well with pointwise equality necessary for caching:

https://dotnetfiddle.net/n55CvJ
